solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One had a huge amount of meat after I'd served up nasty cold soup!

definitions.text: One had a huge amount of meat

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the two letters of I'd are written bottom to top
nasty suggests the words cold soup are spoiled and turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone serves an unpleasant chilled soup after a big meaty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' turns ID into DI; 'nasty' rearranges COLDSOUP into PLODOCUS. 'Meat' here is body mass, not a dinner: this huge dinosaur carried an enormous amount of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplodocus was an enormous sauropod dinosaur, so a single one carried a vast bulk of flesh.

clue.text: Second half of book — a page is given to wild animals

indicators.note: the second half of the four-letter word book is its final two letters

explanation.surface: In the latter part of a book, a page is devoted to wild creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second half of' works on the word itself, not on any book: of its four letters, the last two survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Okapis are shy forest-dwelling mammals of Central Africa, related to giraffes, so they are wild beasts.

clue.text: Part of the globe experienced and whisked round, as you might say

indicators.note: as you might say tells us the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: experienced means knew, and whisked round means whirled, giving the phrase knew whirled

explanation.surface: A traveller's tale of a region they saw and were rushed around.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEW WHIRLED, spoken, matches the answer; the silent K and H vanish in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas are collectively called this, a large region of the Earth's surface.

clue.text: Plant in a garden half eaten? I start to cry

indicators.note: half of the word garden has been eaten away, leaving its first three letters
start to means the opening letter of the word cry

explanation.surface: A gardener sees a plant half devoured by pests and begins to weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half eaten' leaves GAR of GARDEN; 'start to' takes C from 'cry'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agaric is a gill-bearing mushroom, a fungus loosely counted as a plant in older usage.

clue.text: One put into a house with bishops? That could be a severe sentence, look!

definitions.text: One put into a house with bishops

parts.note: a life sentence is the harshest prison term a court can hand down
to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A judge gives a heavy prison term and calls for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The house with bishops is the House of Lords, where Church of England bishops sit alongside appointed members.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer is appointed for their lifetime to the House of Lords, which includes senior bishops.

clue.text: Food in bed is heaven

indicators.note: in indicates the letters sit inside the run of words bed is heaven

explanation.surface: Breakfast in bed is a slice of paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food served at a meal.

clue.text: Delight crossing minimal river, it being this?

definitions.text: Delight crossing minimal river, it being this?

indicators.note: crossing means the first piece stretches across, enclosing the second

parts.note: to tickle is to amuse or delight

indicators.note: minimal reduces the word river to its smallest part, its first letter

explanation.surface: A pleasure crosses a tiny stream, which is itself just a little flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' puts R (from 'minimal river') inside TICKLE. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a minimal river is just this.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin, slow flow of water, exactly what a minimal river amounts to.

clue.text: American novelist's rescue vehicle that sits by the Thames

parts.note: a tower is something that tows, as a breakdown truck does a stranded car
Jack London was an American novelist, so his belongs to London, that is of London

explanation.surface: A breakdown truck belonging to an American writer parked beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novelist's' is read as 'of London', after Jack London, author of The Call of the Wild.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic fortress stands on the north bank of the River Thames in the capital.

clue.text: More dirty and horrible? That is right

parts.note: grim means horrible or grisly
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something grubbier and nastier, and that's correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimier is the comparative of grimy, meaning covered with more dirt.

clue.text: Something intellectually challenging that goes beyond blue-sky thinking?

definitions.text: Something intellectually challenging that goes beyond blue-sky thinking?

parts.words: Something intellectually challenging that goes beyond blue-sky thinking?
parts.note: a byword for a very difficult discipline, here also read literally as the study of craft that fly beyond the blue sky into space

explanation.surface: A demanding field of thought that outstrips imaginative brainstorming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue-sky thinking' is office jargon for unconstrained ideas; literally, the science goes beyond the sky into space.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for any task needing great intellect, from the engineering of spacecraft.

clue.text: Determination shown by weak and sickly prisoner brought before ruler

indicators.note: brought before places the prisoner piece ahead of the ruler piece

parts.note: ill means unwell or sickly
POW stands for prisoner of war
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A frail, ill captive shows resolve when hauled before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is strength of resolve, the same as determination.

clue.text: Set of principles laid down by Elizabeth I contentiously

indicators.note: laid down by points to the letters being set out within the words Elizabeth I contentiously

explanation.surface: A moral code imposed by the Tudor queen amid controversy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a body of moral principles guiding behaviour.

clue.text: Journeys made by newly-weds heading off

indicators.note: heading off removes the head, the first letter, of the word for newly-weds

parts.note: brides are women who have just married

explanation.surface: Trips taken by a just-married couple as they set off on honeymoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides are journeys on horseback or in a vehicle.

clue.text: Carefully chosen soldiers meeting revolutionary beginning to recognise him

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word recognise

parts.note: him refers back to the revolutionary just named, so Che again

explanation.surface: Troops encounter a rebel and begin to identify him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Him' points back to Che, so the name appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherche is French-derived, meaning rare, exquisite or selected with great care.

clue.text: Doing well in Plymouth, say, and not rocking the boat

definitions.note: a phrase describing behaviour, standing for the noun naming that behaviour

indicators.note: in places the doing well piece inside the word for Plymouth

parts.note: Plymouth is an example of a city, in Devon in south-west England
on form means performing well

explanation.surface: A team is thriving in the Devon port and keeping things steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Plymouth as an example of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Conformity is compliance with accepted rules, the opposite of causing trouble or upsetting things.

clue.text: Like gems destined to be placed around church

indicators.note: to be placed around means the destined word wraps the church abbreviation

parts.note: fated means destined
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Jewels fated to be set around a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut gemstones have many flat polished faces, so they are described as having facets.

clue.text: Liqueur — it upset a latter-day Juliet

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word it upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of West Side Story, a modern retelling of Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A drink spilt over a modern-day romantic heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee-flavoured liqueur from Jamaica.

clue.text: Undesirable conditions for section of the orchestra

definitions.meaning: attached ... are hidden conditions that come with an offer
the violins, violas, cellos and basses form one group of players

explanation.surface: A conductor laments the unwelcome terms imposed on the violin players.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: strings attached to a deal, and stringed instruments in an orchestra.

clue.text: Begins journey from Home Counties — is last off

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of is last have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commuter departs from the counties near London, ending up last to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, so they give the compass abbreviation for south-east. 'Off' signals the rearrangement of the two words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship sets sail when it starts its voyage, so the phrase means starts a journey.

clue.text: Attack taking place — killing without hesitation

parts.note: an event that is on is happening

indicators.note: without removes the hesitation sound from the killing word

parts.note: slaughter means killing
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An assault under way, carried out without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes ER from SLAUGHTER, leaving SLAUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, sustained attack.

clue.text: Grand knight that's too much in control

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
over means excessive
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A great knight who is overbearing in command.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or control.

clue.text: Mayonnaise has excellent mixture of oil

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 written as I

indicators.note: mixture of means the letters of oil are mixed

explanation.surface: A good blend of oil makes a mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, gives AI with I standing for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence.

clue.text: I have to follow a bishop to achieve success

indicators.note: to follow sets the I have piece after the bishop piece

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A clergyman's ambition: following a bishop leads to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in the sense of make it means to become successful.

clue.text: Belief in a male divinity overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown turns the whole run of pieces upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: a god is a divinity

explanation.surface: Faith in a masculine god is toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is an established belief or doctrine held unquestioningly.

clue.text: Primitive life form Rex found buried in stone

indicators.note: found buried in means the Rex letter is set inside the stone word

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
R stands for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A fossil of an early organism discovered by a king inside a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a microorganism or the rudimentary origin of life.

clue.text: My servant has been retrained as a church official

indicators.note: retrained suggests the letters of My servant are taught a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A domestic servant has been given new training to serve in a parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestryman is a member of a parish vestry, the body managing church affairs.

clue.text: More socially inept diner is awkward when Queen enters

indicators.note: enters puts the Queen letters into the jumbled diner
awkward implies the letters of diner are clumsily jumbled

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer becomes clumsier when the monarch walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges DINER into NDIER (one arrangement); 'enters' puts ER in, giving NERDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerdy means awkwardly obsessive and lacking social graces, so this is its comparative.

clue.text: One's asked to come home before six to what sounds like tea

indicators.note: before places the home piece ahead of the six piece

parts.note: in means at home
VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: what sounds like signals that tea is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like TEE

explanation.surface: Someone is asked round home before six for an afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitee is a person who has received an invitation.
